question: What primary operational problem does Continuous Integration solve?
options: High server hosting costs caused by unused infrastructure.
Lack of relational database schema backups before deployments.
Integration friction and late bug discovery caused by long-lived unmerged code.
Slow network speeds during large file downloads.
explanation: Continuous Integration prevents integration friction and late defect discovery by forcing frequent code merges and automated build validations.

question: Which of the following describes the Lead Time for Changes metric?
options: The time elapsed from code commit check-in to deployment in production.
The duration of the daily engineering standup meeting.
The total time spent writing unit tests for a new feature.
The CPU execution time required by a CI runner.
explanation: Lead Time for Changes measures the total pipeline velocity from the initial commit up to running live in production.

question: How does technical deployment differ from functional release?
options: Deployment is done by developers; release is done by database administrators.
Deployment occurs in production; release only occurs in staging.
Deployment requires manual approval; release is always automated.
Deployment installs code in an environment; release makes features accessible to end users.
explanation: Decoupling deployment (technical installation) from release (user access exposure) reduces deployment risk and enables continuous delivery.

question: Which pair of DORA metrics explicitly measures software delivery stability?
options: Deployment Frequency and Lead Time for Changes.
Change Failure Rate and Failed Deployment Recovery Time.
Code Review Speed and Test Coverage Percentage.
Build Execution Time and CPU Usage.
explanation: Change Failure Rate and Failed Deployment Recovery Time (MTTR) are the two official DORA stability metrics.

question: What is an immediate requirement when a Continuous Integration pipeline build fails on the main branch?
options: Bypass the pipeline and deploy the code manually.
Delete the failing automated test from the repository.
Stop new feature work and fix the build immediately.
Wait until the end of the month to investigate log files.
explanation: Maintaining a healthy build requires fixing broken main pipelines immediately so the entire team can continue integrating safely.
